- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.11) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 5–7 days.  
- If recent price history shows strong downward momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops) and sentiment is neutral or negative, model often underestimates; adjust up by 1–3% to account for mean reversion.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots in the following 7–14 days; apply a “cool-down” correction: subtract 1–3% from forecast for next 7 days.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.28) and price is trending down, model often fails to recognize the depth of the drop; forecast should be adjusted downward by 2–4% for next 5–10 days.  
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate early in the horizon (first 7–10 days) when sentiment is positive; apply a “lag correction” by reducing first 5–7 days’ forecast by 1–2% relative to 18-day history.  
- When sentiment is volatile or mixed (±0.11), model often fails to capture short-term reversals; use sentiment-weighted smoothing: if sentiment > 0.11, apply 10% weight to recent 3-day average; if sentiment < 0.11, apply 15% weight to recent 3-day average.
